effective.basis: Old state: UDE official card rulings (Sangan/Witch: 'If you have no eligible monsters, your opponent gets to see your Deck to verify', captured 2005-06-16) through Konami's own per-set rulings documents - Machina Mayhem (2010-04-06, 18 days before the Edison snapshot), Starstrike Blast (2010-11-16), Storm of Ragnarok (2011-02-02). New state: KDE-US Tournament Policy section 'Card/Hand/Deck Verification' forbids verifying the opponent's Deck (first located capture 2019-04-03; still current in v2.5, 2025-09-05). No dated announcement of the change was found, so the interval 2011-02-02 .. 2019-04-03 stays open.

changes.historical_text: FLIP: Select 1 Trap Card from your Deck and place it on top of your Deck. If "Necrovalley" is on the field, you can add the selected Trap Card to your hand instead.
changes.summary: Period procedure, not a text erratum: the goat script's only behavioural difference from the modern one is an else-branch calling Duel.GoatConfirm(tp,LOCATION_DECK), so a FLIP search that finds no Trap in the Deck is proven by revealing the Deck, which is then shuffled; the modern script simply does nothing on a whiff. Selection, the "Necrovalley" add-to-hand alternative and the place-on-top-of-Deck branch are byte-identical in both scripts.

review.notes: Chain starts at lineage v1 (DR1-EN018, Dark Revelation Volume 1, 2005-03-19), which the goat cdb text matches exactly. v0 (PGD-070, 2003-07-18) predates the baseline and differs only in wording ('is active on the field', 'add the selected card'). The trailing v1 -> v2 rewording (SS01-ENB11, 2019-01-24: 'Select' -> 'Choose', 'Trap Card' -> 'Trap', clause restructured with 'or,') is cosmetic and is not recorded as a change. The FLIP effect is mandatory in both scripts and neither has an activation-condition check to relax, so this variant encodes only (A) the failed-search verification procedure, not (B) any relaxed activation condition.
